title: SR-1.34 A daemon start waits long enough for a slow machine, and a hook says 'starting'
request: Closes the open follow-up 'Raise the daemon start wait' (docs/scope-one/RECONCILIATION.md, found 1 Nov 2026; not in the gap register of the investment analysis): startDaemon and ensureDaemon wait 6000 ms (src/cli/daemon.mjs:69 and :76), then stop the daemon (daemon.mjs:91-92). On a slow Windows runner the daemon has not reached listen by then (src/server/main.mjs opens the vault at line 28 before listen; its 'cannot listen' line is at line 45), so it is stopped before it can write its log: the start reports 'did not start', the listen-error line is never written, and a session-start hook shows 'Memev is not reachable' instead of the resume card (hooks.mjs:192). Measured on the Windows job of ci.yml on main: the daemon did not serve within 6 s in 8 runs of doctor MEM-006 AC02, the longest whole-test duration of a failed start is 12.7 s (run 41244882353, job 124666127747), so the ceiling is 30 s, 2 x that rounded up (see requirement 6; the logs carry no start-to-serving time, only that it exceeded 6 s, so the 12.7 s is a proxy). Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: SR-1.01, SR-1.24 (both signed in their second versions and left untouched: src/cli/daemon.mjs is already in the scope of SR-1.01 T3 and SR-1.24 T1, and neither names the start wait). Sequenced with SR-1.01 and SR-1.24, which change src/cli/daemon.mjs. Sensitive path: none (the oplog is not touched).

tasks.title: A start waits long enough for a slow machine, and a hook says 'starting'
requirements: src/cli/daemon.mjs exports START_WAIT_MS = 30000 and uses it as the default wait of ensureDaemon and startDaemon in place of 6000. The wait is a ceiling, not a delay: the loop already returns as soon as this vault's daemon answers and stops as soon as the child exits with anything but 3, and that does not change. When the wait ends the daemon is still stopped, as today (daemon.mjs:91-92), so a start that gives up leaves no daemon that comes up unreported

the hook path keeps a short wait: src/cli/hooks.mjs defines HOOK_START_WAIT_MS = 4000 and passes it to ensureDaemon (hooks.mjs:84). Hooks still fail open and exit 0. A start made by a hook whose short wait ends does NOT stop the daemon it began, because stopping it would make 'still starting' untrue and a slow machine would never get a daemon from hooks alone: startDaemon takes an option for this (for example { keep: true }) that skips the stop at the end of the wait and leaves the child to come up; the stop at the end of a start made by memev start, memev init or memev restart is unchanged. A daemon that is kept must still end: see requirement 7

when the daemon is still starting (daemon.lock names a live pid and the daemon has not answered), the session-start card says 'starting' and names no error, instead of 'Memev is not reachable right now' (hooks.mjs:192 at main b5932d3); when no daemon is starting the existing text stays

memev start and memev init print one line to stderr when a start is still waiting after 6 s: 'Memev is still starting; waiting up to 30 s (see <path of daemon.log>)'. Quiet callers print nothing. init calls startDaemon with quiet:true (main.mjs:272), so the line comes from a callback or option that init and start pass, not from the quiet flag
ensureDaemon in mcp-stdio.mjs, bus-cli.mjs and memev start keep the long default; nothing outside src/cli/daemon.mjs, src/cli/hooks.mjs, src/cli/main.mjs and src/server/main.mjs changes behaviour

the ceiling comes from measurement and is recorded here, not guessed. The Windows job's CI logs on main (the ci.yml runs 41197857234 to 41277608997, 64 job attempts, 19 failed) hold no daemon start-to-serving time: a test reports its own duration and a pass or fail, and the daemon log is not in the log. What the logs do give is a lower bound: in every one of the 8 failures of doctor test MEM-006 AC02 the daemon had not served within the 6 s wait, and startDaemon then stops it (daemon.mjs:91-92), so how long it would have needed cannot be seen. The proxy used is the longest whole-test duration of a failed start that no poll lengthened: 12.7 s (run 41244882353 attempt 1, job 124666127747), which holds the vault creation, the 6 s wait and two onboarding runs; the other unpolled failures took 7.6 s, 8.3 s, 8.4 s, 8.9 s, 9.8 s and 11.0 s, and the one with the 20 s poll took 30.6 s (run 41274568215 attempt 1, job 124754017252). 2 x 12.7 s = 25.4 s, rounded up to the clean number 30 s. This is a proxy for a start time, not a measured one, and it is flagged as such: the pull request that adds this spec lists every value with its run and job. The ceiling is to be re-set from a real start-to-serving time once one is logged: requirement 9 and criterion T1-c16 make the daemon log it

a kept daemon that never comes up ends on its own: src/server/main.mjs arms a watchdog when it begins. If the daemon has not reached listen by the ceiling (START_WAIT_MS, or MEMEV_START_WAIT_MS when the parent passes it, which the tests use to shorten it), the watchdog removes daemon.lock and exits non-zero; a daemon that fails earlier exits at once on that failure, as today (codes 3, 4, 5). No daemon lingers for ever, so a hook cannot leave a process that neither serves nor ends. The watchdog is cleared when the daemon reaches listen

the SR-1.01 one-writer rule holds while a start is in progress: a start that finds daemon.lock naming a live pid does not spawn a second daemon, it waits for that pid's daemon to answer (within its own wait) and reuses it. A caller that did not begin the daemon never stops it when its wait ends (only the caller that began a daemon stops it, as today, unless that start was kept). The lock (daemon.lock, main.mjs:20-26) still arbitrates two daemons that start at the same instant, with exit code 3 for the loser

the daemon logs a real start-to-serving time so the next revision has measurements: the 'serving' line in .memev/daemon.log ends with 'in <N> ms', N counted from the start of the process (process.uptime) to listen, and the 'cannot listen' line carries the same count. The 30 s ceiling stays and stays flagged as a proxy until a logged number replaces it

the retry that doctor MEM-006 AC02 carries (pull request #372, a workaround for this item, comment pointing at SR-1.01 and SR-1.24) is removed by this task, and test/start-window-listen-error.test.mjs, which states why a wait cannot see the line, stays
